reviews.comment: He seemed kind of arrogant to me and like he intentionally answered questions in a confusing way with big words/phrases just to sound smarter. I essentially taught myself the material in this class because of that. Not a horrible professor but I would avoid him looking back.

Prof. Harrop once claimed that he wants his students to play an active role in their learning, which would be a nice sentiment if he weren't an awful lecturer who leaves you no choice but to learn the material on your own. His lectures are wordy and confusing, as are his answers to questions. He takes pride in how challenging it is to make an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: weekly quizzes that are kinda confusing, as are tests, but any philosophy class kinda uses trippy wording I feel like. He canceled class a lot/was going thru stuff so feel like he was more lenient with our class bc of that. overall interesting/good!
His quizzes will be difficult and low score, but if you try on papers and go to office hours an A is definitely possible

reviews.comment: Don't take this class. Prof Harrop does not care about his students and will take 3 weeks to get back to your emails. There are barely any grades in the gradebook and makes the class to where you just barely pass the class and its almost impossible to have an A. The tests are impossible and I've never seen so many questions asked DURING an exam.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is honestly a caring professor that is willing to match your needs. There is a quiz once a week that goes over the material covered that week. These quizzes should be your worst grade but it's fine as long as you do good on the papers. Papers can be difficult but he is super helpful. Not the easiest class but definitely doable.
reviews.ratingTags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class
